points: The report examines whether investors are right to assume that today’s record profitability will fade.

items.title: Making underwater radiated noise measurement practical for the world fleet
points: Along with ICS, IPTA and RINA, we have co-sponsored a proposal to MEPC 85 aimed at making underwater radiated noise (URN) measurement practical and affordable for the world fleet.
The IMO’s Revised Guidelines (MEPC.1/Circ.906/Rev.1) prefer direct measurement to establish a ship’s URN baseline, and class society quiet ship notations normally require it.
The problem Dedicated sea trials cost an estimated USD 30,000–50,000 directly, and USD 40,000–250,000 per ship once diversion and lost revenue are included.
Across a fleet of around 100,000 ships, one round of measurements could cost USD 4–25 billion, and repeat measurements may be needed.
Ship-specific data checking and reporting would add around USD 4,424 per ship • An ISO “Measurement of Opportunity” standard is needed for consistent results.

Dry weather is likely to prevail over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema till November 16, with light to moderate rain likely at isolated places over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on November 17.
Squally weather with wind speeds of 45-55 kmph, gusting to 65 kmph, is likely along and off the Andhra Pradesh coast on November 17.
Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority Managing Director Prakhar Jain said that, as per current forecasts, the system is likely to move towards north Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh coasts.

items.title: ICFAI honours undergraduate toppers at 16th graduation ceremony
points: The ICFAI Foundation for Higher Education (IFHE) held its 16th undergraduate graduation ceremony at Aarya Convention on Shankarpally Road on November 12, with students from various schools receiving gold medals and awards for academic excellence.

items.title: CMA CGM Net Profit More Than Triples to $2.32 Billion as Freight Rates Surge
points: French shipping giant CMA CGM more than tripled its third-quarter net profit as higher container freight rates and strong cargo volumes boosted earnings amid ongoing disruptions to global shipping routes in the Middle East.

The Marseille-based group reported Friday that net income attributable to the group climbed to $2.32 billion in the third quarter of 2026, up from $760 million a year earlier, an increase of approximately 205%.
Revenue rose 31.1% to $18.4 billion, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) jumped 61.6% to $4.78 billion.
The group’s EBITDA margin improved to 25.9%, compared with 21% in the same period last year.
Shipping revenue surged 37.3% to $12.3 billion, supported by a 30% increase in average revenue per container to $1,891 per TEU.
CMA CGM also expanded its terminal network through a partnership involving Terminal 4 at Saudi Arabia’s Port of Jeddah and the acquisition of a 49% stake in Morocco’s Nador Container Terminal.

items.title: 3 Hours After 3 Years: Punjab MP Amritpal Singh's Interim Bail Comes With 8 Conditions
points: Amritpal Singh, the Lok Sabha member from Punjab who has been jailed since 2023, will walk out of Assam's Dibrugarh prison this weekend and be taken to his home state, but this interim bail comes with a set of eight stringent terms.

The MP from Khadoor Sahib, who has faced allegations of stoking separatism, has been allowed to attend his grandmother Charan Kaur's cremation for three hours on Saturday, though it may be delayed due to the long travel from Assam to Punjab.

On Friday, the Amritsar district and sessions court, where a specific case against him is being heard, allowed the Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De) chief to join the cremation on November 14 "in police custody with high security for 3 hours only".
Amritpal Singh has been held in Assam's Dibrugarh Central Jail for more than three-and-a-half years.
If Amritpal Singh reaches Punjab as the court ordered, it will be his first public appearance since his arrest in 2023.

items.title: Property Dealer Shot Dead In Haryana: 4 Bullets Hit Him, 13 Shells Found
points: A property dealer was shot dead in Haryana's Gohana on Friday evening.
Bijender Pehal sustained four bullet injuries, while 13 empty cartridges were recovered from the crime scene, officials said.
Hours later, a person identifying himself as Virender Charan claimed responsibility for Pehal's murder in a Facebook post.
Claiming to be associated with the Arvind Gilli-Rana and Rohit Godara gang, Charan described the murder as revenge for an alleged attack on one of their associates in 2021.
Pehal runs Shivam Properties, a real estate firm on Rohtak Road.
In his social media post, Charan alleged that Pehal had attacked their associate Rampal Baroda in 2021 and subsequently assaulted him again when he was returning from hospital after treatment.
Pehal, who originally belonged to Ghumar village in the Ganaur area, had been living in Adarsh Nagar in Gohana for a considerable period and was engaged in the property business.

The awards, presented in Ho Chi Minh City in Vietnam, recognise television programmes and broadcasters from across Asia, including Taiwan, China, Japan, Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore.

His complaints to the authorities were allegedly ignored, even when he bled from injuries sustained during the assault.

After he came out of the jail, his father approached the police, who filed a first information report (FIR) against 19 people, including the jail superintendent, the jail hospital medical officer and the ward in-charge.
The victim's complaint states that he was drugged, made to wear a saree and sexually assaulted by inmates.
When he complained, his letter was torn up, and he was denied medical treatment.
Per the complaint, he was sexually assaulted by the group on three occasions -- on Mahashivratri, Ram Navami, and Sarhul.

items.title: "Dark Pattern": Ola Fined Rs 10 Lakh Over Pre-Ride 'Tip' Feature
points: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of Rs 10 lakh on ANI Technologies Private Limited, which operates ride-hailing platform Ola, for soliciting additional payments from customers before their journeys were completed.
The regulator said the pre-ride 'tip' or 'add-on' feature misled consumers, amounted to an unfair trade practice and employed a dark pattern.
The CCPA held this amounted to concealment of material information under Section 2(28)(iv) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
The suggested amounts were generated on an undisclosed basis and rose from Rs 10-Rs 40 in May 2025 to as much as Rs 140, while the interface allowed payments of up to Rs 499.
The practice also contravened Clause 14.15 of the Motor Vehicles Aggregators Guidelines, 2025, which allows a tipping feature only after the journey is completed, the CCPA said.
It noted that Ola continued showing the prompt even after the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways clarified on August 11, 2026, that such prompts could not be displayed before the ride ended.

items.title: Hapag-Lloyd Profit Surges as Freight Rates Rise, Red Sea Services Return
points: German container shipping giant Hapag-Lloyd reported a sharp increase in third-quarter earnings as higher freight rates more than offset rising operating costs tied to the Middle East conflict and widespread port congestion.

The Hamburg-based carrier reported Thursday that third-quarter net profit jumped to $999 million, up from $172 million a year earlier, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) nearly doubled to $1.73 billion.
Revenue climbed 26% to $6.88 billion, driven largely by stronger freight rates and high vessel utilization across its global container network.
The company’s average freight rate increased 28% to $1,808 per twenty-foot equivalent unit (TEU), compared with $1,413 in the third quarter of 2025.
Its operating profit forecast was also raised to between $2.0 billion and $2.4 billion, compared with an earlier range of $1.25 billion to $1.75 billion.
Earlier this month, Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd announced that their joint ME1 India–Europe service, known as IOS at Hapag-Lloyd, would switch from the Cape of Good Hope to the Suez Canal.
